#### `raw.airtoxscreen__tract_risk`

EPA AirToxScreen 2018/2019 assessment, by-source-group cancer risk file ('...CancerRisk_by_tract_srcgrp.xlsx'), landed verbatim and whole per assessment_year. Carries national, state, county AND census-tract rows (module docstring); measure.observation derives only the real tract rows. Public domain (17 U.S.C. Sec 105; https://edg.epa.gov/epa_data_license.html).

**Sorted by:** `assessment_year, fips, tract`  

| Column | Type | Required | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | string |  | USPS 2-letter state abbreviation, as published (also "US" for the one national-total row). |
| `epa_region` | string |  | EPA region name (e.g. 'EPA Region 4'), or 'Entire US' on the national row. |
| `county` | string |  | County name, or 'Entire State'/'Entire US' on the state/national aggregate rows. |
| `fips` | string |  | 5-digit county FIPS code (state rows: state FIPS + "000"; the national row: "00000"). |
| `tract` | string |  | 11-digit tract FIPS code for a real tract row; the county's own code + "000000" for a county-aggregate row, or "00000000000"/state-FIPS+"000000000" for the national/state rows (module docstring: derive uses only real tract rows, `tract NOT LIKE '%000000'`). |
| `population` | string |  | Resident population the estimate covers, as published. |
| `total_cancer_risk` | string |  | Total modeled lifetime cancer risk from ambient air toxics (all source groups, all pollutants combined), chances per million, as published under the header 'Total Cancer Risk (per million)'. Published rounded to a small set of risk bins (5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 20, 30, ..., 100, 200, 300, 400 -- verified against the real file), not a continuous value; that rounding is EPA's own publication convention, not a landing defect. #### `raw.ers__food_access_sram`

USDA ERS Food Access Research Atlas, SNAP-authorized Retailer Access Map (SRAM) landed verbatim and whole, every published column from the General Tract Characteristics and Straight-Line Distance files joined on CensusTract20, one row per 2020 census tract per edition (issue #112). Driving (Network-Based) Distance file not landed -- a new methodology axis with no analog in raw.ers__food_access, see ers_food_access.py docstring. Public domain (17 U.S.C. Sec 105).

### `geography` — Units, vintages, crosswalks, aliases — the spine every fact joins through.

#### `geography.alias`

FIPS renames and re-codings that are NOT boundary changes (SPEC.md § geography.alias, #26): a join on an old code resolves through here to the current one instead of dropping (SPEC.md Acceptance B). Real boundary changes (splits, merges, Connecticut's planning regions) belong to geography.crosswalk (#25) instead, since a 1:1 alias would misrepresent them.

**Business key:** `old_geo_id, new_geo_id`  
**Sorted by:** `old_geo_id, new_geo_id`  

| Column | Type | Required | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `old_geo_id` | string | yes | geography.unit-style id ('county:<fips>') before the change. Part of the business key together with new_geo_id. Carries no vintage — unlike geography.unit, an alias is a pure code mapping a join resolves regardless of which vintage the observation came from. |
| `new_geo_id` | string | yes | geography.unit-style id ('county:<fips>') after the change. Part of the business key together with old_geo_id. |
| `effective_year` | int | yes | Calendar year the change took effect, e.g. 2015. |
| `change_type` | string | yes | One of: recode (code changed, name did not), rename (name changed, code did not — not useful for resolving a join, since old_geo_id would equal new_geo_id, so none are seeded), recode_and_rename (both changed, e.g. Shannon -> Oglala Lakota County). |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Name before the change. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Name after the change. |
| `source` | string | yes | Asserting provider, e.g. 'CENSUS_COUNTY_CHANGES'. Part of every writer's merge scope, so a second source of aliases (NHGIS, say) could stack here without retiring this one's rows. |
| `source_url` | string | yes | The page this row's change was documented on. |
| `note` | string |  | Citation: the exact source sentence this row was transcribed from. |
| `valid_from` | string | yes | The Cancer Basemap release from which this version of the record is valid. A row is one *version*: any change to any attribute closes the previous row and opens a new one, so the value here is not necessarily when the record first existed. It is when Cancer Basemap first carried this version, not when the source published it. |
| `valid_to` | string |  | The Cancer Basemap release at which this version stopped being current, exclusive. NULL means this is the current version — it does not mean unknown. Queries wanting current data must filter on valid_to IS NULL; queries wanting release R want valid_from <= R AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > R). This is a Cancer Basemap release, not the date the source changed the record. |

### `provenance` — What each Cancer Basemap release was built from, and how we know.

#### `provenance.lineage`

Table- and column-level lineage DAG, one row per edge, captured at ingest with sqlglot (cancerbasemap.lineage, #140). Rebuildable from each ingest's own SQL, so merge.write scopes it on (release, job, to_table) -- no Type 2 history, same as provenance.release. The table-level DAG is `SELECT DISTINCT from_table, to_table`; never stored twice, since a table-level-only row (to_column NULL) is written only for a pair no column-level edge already covers.

**Sorted by:** `release, job, to_table, to_column`  

| Column | Type | Required | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `release` | string | yes | Cancer Basemap release whose ingest recorded this edge. FK provenance.release.release. |
| `job` | string | yes | The ingest module that produced this edge, by its module name (e.g. 'ers_rucc', 'places'). |
| `to_table` | string | yes | Target table, dotted namespace.table (e.g. 'measure.observation'). |
| `to_column` | string |  | Target column. NULL means this edge is table-level only: known to feed to_table, but not narrowed to one column -- e.g. an output built in Python from a query's rows rather than by the query's own column aliases (measure.definition from PLACES' MeasureId lookup). |
| `to_variable` | string |  | For a long table keyed by a literal value per row (measure_id in measure.observation; a future typed.*__long's variable, #139), the specific key value this edge applies to, when the source SQL states it as a literal in that branch. NULL when the table isn't keyed this way, or when the key is a computed expression rather than a literal -- PLACES' measure_id is built from two columns, not asserted as one value per branch, so its edges legitimately carry no to_variable. |
| `from_table` | string | yes | Source: a catalog table identifier, or -- when from_kind='url' -- the upstream URL a raw table was landed from (the DAG's root). |
| `from_column` | string |  | Source column. NULL for a table-level-only edge or a from_kind='url' root edge. |
| `from_kind` | string | yes | 'table' when from_table is a catalog table identifier, 'url' when it is the upstream URL a raw table was landed from. |
| `expression` | string |  | The SQL expression that produced to_column from from_column, verbatim from sqlglot (e.g. 'CASE WHEN EP_POV150 = -999 THEN NULL ELSE EP_POV150 END'). NULL for a table-level-only or url-root edge. |
| `code_version` | string | yes | git sha of cancerbasemap (short form) at the time this edge was recorded, or the installed package version when git is unavailable. |

#### `provenance.release`

One row per (Cancer Basemap release, source, source_version): what this release was built from. This is what makes a release reproducible — resolve it here to each source's own version, then query each table at that release. Durable by design: unlike Iceberg snapshot summaries it does not expire. Keyed on source_version too (#78) so landing several source releases of one source under one catalog release keeps a row for each.

**Business key:** `release, source, source_version`  
**Sorted by:** `release, source, source_version`  

| Column | Type | Required | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `release` | string | yes | Cancer Basemap release, YYYY.MM with zero-padded corrections YYYY.MM.NN. Zero-padded because '2026.10.10' sorts before '2026.10.2' and release ordering would otherwise invert. |
| `source` | string | yes | Source key, e.g. scp, places, acs. |
| `source_version` | string | yes | The upstream version in the SOURCE'S OWN vocabulary, never normalised. Part of the business key together with release and source (#78): several source releases can land under one catalog release, and keying on (release, source) alone kept only the last one landed. Always populated — merge.manifest defaults it to the retrieval date when the source publishes no version label of its own, so it is never NULL. |
| `version_method` | string | yes | How the version was determined: release_number, http_last_modified, etag, ftp_index_probe, retrieval_date, unavailable. 'unavailable' is a legitimate value — a source that publishes no version is recorded as such, never given a fabricated one. |
| `retrieved_at` | string | yes | UTC timestamp at which the source was fetched. |
| `url` | string |  | Canonical URL fetched. |
| `checksum` | string |  | SHA-256 of the retrieved bytes, where computed. |
| `row_count` | int |  | Rows landed from this source, as a cheap integrity check. |
